questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then you may go when the way is clear.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass if you are in the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane and let any traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or if emergency help is not there yet. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never stop just to look at an accident.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive with care near bicyclists.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing rules, and other driving rules.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: When should you leave more space in front of your car than usual?

options.text: When stopped on a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopped on a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when you stop on an uphill slope. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic starts, you will have more room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: Which tip does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Do not look into oncoming headlights. Your pupils shrink when you look at bright lights. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn.
All traffic must go straight.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is ahead. A road will join from the right side.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gases from your vehicle. A leak allows harmful fumes into the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away to prevent poisoning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction to drive on a one-way street. You must follow the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do at an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, yield to vehicles from your right. Always be prepared to yield. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, then left again.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge in the direction the arrow points.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left, but yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left, but yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left. However, oncoming traffic has a green light. You must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency signals on. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: Turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
Stop turning and go straight.
Turn with the right-of-way.
You no longer need to turn that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. But you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the other vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road. This keeps the bright lights from blinding you and helps you see the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Which traffic light means: stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when clear?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when the way is clear.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When should you slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Before entering the exit ramp.
After you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: Your car's accelerator gets stuck open on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition carefully. Move the key only enough to stop the engine, not so far that the steering wheel locks. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign means you must stop and yield the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge their distance and speed, so stay alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep steady speed.
Follow closer to other cars.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control.
